name: Dar Al Arkan

summary.text: Dar Al Arkan Real Estate Development Company is a Riyadh property developer founded in 1994 by Yousef Al Shelash, who is its chairman, and listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul, code 4300) in 2007. It is the parent of Dar Global PLC, its international arm, which it listed in London in February 2023 while holding 88 percent of the shares. Through Dar Global and directly it has partnered with the Trump Organization on Trump-branded projects including Trump Tower Jeddah, the $1 billion Trump Plaza Jeddah within its Manhattan-style masterplan on King Abdulaziz Road, and the Wadi Safar golf project near Riyadh; Donald Trump's financial disclosures reported about $21.9 million (2024) and $25.8 million (2025) of licensing income from Dar Al Arkan and Dar Global. The Dar Global file on this site holds the project list and the disclosures; this file holds the parent company.

facts.claim: Forbes Middle East records that Yousef Al Shelash founded Dar Al Arkan in Riyadh in 1994 and that the company was listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) in 2007; he is its founder and chairman.

facts.claim: Dar Al Arkan announced in September 2025 a Manhattan-style masterplan on King Abdulaziz Road in Jeddah featuring Trump Plaza, a $1 billion mixed-use project developed with the Trump Organization, following Trump Tower Jeddah, a 47-storey SR 2 billion tower on the Jeddah Corniche.

facts.claim: Forbes reported in May 2025 that Dar Al Arkan had at least six projects in the works with the Trump Organization across Dubai, Oman, Qatar and Saudi Arabia, and quoted Eric Trump calling Al Shelash a member of the Trump family; Al Shelash attended a lunch with President Trump during the May 2025 Riyadh visit, and the White House said there were no conflicts of interest.
facts.quote: Dar Al Arkan now has at least six projects in the works with the Trump Organization, spanning hotels, golf clubs, villas and luxury apartments in Dubai, Oman, Qatar and Saudi Arabia

facts.claim: Forbes reported in June 2025 that Donald Trump's financial disclosure covering 2024 listed about $21.9 million in revenue from Dar Al Arkan; the 2026 disclosure covering 2025, as analysed by CNBC and reported by The Real Deal, showed $25.8 million in licensing income from Dar Al Arkan and Dar Global.
